prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a NEW 1977 Jackie Leven portrait for an existing dark illustrated timeline. The previous 1977 drawing is being replaced because it no longer matches the series.

REFERENCE ROLES: Image 1 is the ORIGINAL photograph. Jackie is the large man closest to the camera, in the foreground on the LEFT, with swept-back dark hair, open-neck dark shirt and a direct upward gaze. Use ONLY this man's face and physique. Do not depict any of the three other band members. Image 2 is the CURRENT APPROVED SERIES STYLE AND TONAL reference only: match its restrained neutral greys, rough dry-brush drawing, calm broad facial planes and black background. Do not borrow its facial proportions, long hair, moustache, beard, gaze or clothes.

Create a fresh drawing directly from Jackie in image 1. Frame his head, shoulders and upper chest in an upright 4:5 portrait. Retain the slightly forward-leaning shoulder posture and the head lifted towards the viewer from a subtly higher viewpoint. His serious direct look carries the confrontational energy of a young rock musician, without inventing a snarl, heroic pose or extra aggression. Preserve the distinctive actual facial anatomy: high broad exposed forehead, true hairline, eyebrows and asymmetrical eye shapes, heavy lids, nose width and tip, relatively thin natural lips, full cheek and jaw contours. Clean-shaven except for the visible sideburns. Do not idealize, slim his face, sharpen his jaw, hollow his cheeks, enlarge the eyes, smooth away asymmetry or turn him into a generic model. Faithful, unpolished likeness is more important than attractiveness.

Hair exactly in the character of the original: lifted and swept BACK from the high forehead, darker longer ends behind the ears and towards the nape. Not the loose parted long hair of the former 1977 illustration, not the 1971 reference's hair, no extra glamorous flowing volume. His dark broad shirt collar and open neckline are retained, with any fine checks merely suggested. Lower chest and shoulders can be loosely reconstructed within this simple portrait framing. No visible hands are needed.

Completely recompose the setting: a nearly empty anthracite background #0d0f12 with quiet broken brush marks. No ladder, stairs, railings, street, bricks, band members or recognizable arrangement from the source photo.

Match image 2's hand-drawn tonal language closely. Rough dry-brush ink with several broad coherent grey value groups, selective irregular hatching and imperfect brush endings. Face planes readable and subdued; approximately #777a7d for the brightest substantial skin plane, with darker midtones and deep charcoal shadows. Hair mostly dark negative space with a handful of sweeping broken strokes. Shirt and shoulders increasingly dissolve into the background in rough unfinished edges. Anatomical features remain precisely placed but fine skin and hair detail are simplified. Avoid smooth photographic gradients, dense pores, oil-paint mosaic texture, gloss, vector cutouts or an added digital photo filter. Do not create a black-on-white drawing.

Strictly NEUTRAL grey, charcoal and black, no sepia, brown, beige, cream or colour tint. Do not let the original's bright forehead and bare chest become white patches. Natural positive lighting, dark pupils and nostrils within grey face planes. The result should sit as quietly in a dark webpage as image 2, with the raw presence of the original young man.
One standalone 4:5 portrait, full top of hair with dark breathing room, no text, logo, frame or signature.
